This vignette collects short, self-contained recipes for common
`neuroarchive` workflows. Each recipe creates its own data and temp
files so you can run any section independently.

```{r}
library(neuroarchive)
```

## Quantization and Lazy Reading

Write data with quantization and read a temporal subset lazily (without
loading the entire file into memory).

```{r quant_lazy}
x <- array(rnorm(128), dim = c(4, 4, 4, 2))
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")

write_lna(x, tmp, transforms = "quant")

# Open lazily and read a single timepoint
r <- read_lna(tmp, lazy = TRUE)
r$subset(time_idx = 1)
subset_data <- r$data()
r$close()

cat(sprintf("Full data: %s\n", paste(dim(x), collapse = " x ")))
cat(sprintf("Subset shape: %s\n", paste(dim(subset_data), collapse = " x ")))
```

## PCA Compression Pipeline

Combine PCA basis decomposition with quantization for higher compression.

```{r pca_pipeline}
set.seed(1)
x <- array(rnorm(4 * 4 * 4 * 10), dim = c(4, 4, 4, 10))
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")

write_lna(x, tmp,
          transforms = c("basis", "quant"),
          transform_params = list(basis = list(k = 5)))

handle <- read_lna(tmp)
recon <- handle$stash$input

cat(sprintf("Original range: [%.2f, %.2f]\n", min(x), max(x)))
cat(sprintf("Correlation: %.4f\n",
            cor(as.vector(x), as.vector(recon))))
```

## ROI and Time Slicing

Use a binary mask to read only voxels in a region of interest,
combined with time indexing.

```{r roi_slicing}
set.seed(2)
x <- array(rnorm(4 * 4 * 4 * 6), dim = c(4, 4, 4, 6))
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")

write_lna(x, tmp,
          transforms = "quant",
          transform_params = list(quant = list(bits = 8)))

r <- read_lna(tmp, lazy = TRUE)

# Create a binary ROI mask (keep ~half the voxels)
roi <- array(runif(64) > 0.5, dim = c(4, 4, 4))
r$subset(roi_mask = roi, time_idx = 1:3)
roi_data <- r$data()
r$close()

cat(sprintf("Voxels in ROI: %d\n", sum(roi)))
cat(sprintf("ROI subset shape: %s\n",
            paste(dim(roi_data), collapse = " x ")))
```

## Temporal Transform (DCT)

Project time series onto a DCT basis for temporal compression.

```{r temporal_dct}
set.seed(3)
x <- array(rnorm(4 * 4 * 4 * 20), dim = c(4, 4, 4, 20))
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")

write_lna(x, tmp,
          transforms = c("temporal", "quant"),
          transform_params = list(
            temporal = list(kind = "dct", n_basis = 10),
            quant = list(bits = 8)
          ))

handle <- read_lna(tmp)
recon <- handle$stash$input

cat(sprintf("Correlation: %.4f\n",
            cor(as.vector(x), as.vector(recon))))
cat(sprintf("File size: %.1f KB\n",
            file.info(tmp)$size / 1024))
```

## Delta Transform (Lossless)

Delta encoding computes first-order differences along the time axis.
It is lossless and often helps subsequent quantization.

```{r delta_transform}
set.seed(4)
x <- array(rnorm(4 * 4 * 4 * 8), dim = c(4, 4, 4, 8))
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")

write_lna(x, tmp, transforms = "delta")

handle <- read_lna(tmp)
recon <- handle$stash$input

cat(sprintf("Max reconstruction error: %e\n",
            max(abs(as.vector(x) - as.vector(recon)))))
```

## Haar Octave Wavelet

The `spat.haar_octwave` transform performs a 3D Haar wavelet analysis
using Morton-curve ordering. Small detail coefficients can be
thresholded for lossy spatial compression.

```{r haar_octwave}
set.seed(5)
x <- array(rnorm(4 * 4 * 4 * 4), dim = c(4, 4, 4, 4))
mask <- array(TRUE, dim = c(4, 4, 4))
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")

write_lna(x, tmp,
          mask = mask,
          transforms = "spat.haar_octwave",
          transform_params = list(
            spat.haar_octwave = list(levels = 2)
          ))

handle <- read_lna(tmp)
recon <- handle$stash$input

# Spatial transforms return a time-by-voxel matrix
cat(sprintf("Output shape: %s\n", paste(dim(recon), collapse = " x ")))
cat(sprintf("File size: %.1f KB\n", file.info(tmp)$size / 1024))
```

## Validate an LNA File

`validate_lna()` checks file structure, schema conformance, and
SHA-256 checksums.

```{r validate}
set.seed(6)
x <- array(rnorm(4 * 4 * 4 * 2), dim = c(4, 4, 4, 2))
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")

write_lna(x, tmp, transforms = "quant")

# Returns TRUE when the file is sound
is_valid <- validate_lna(tmp)
cat(sprintf("Valid: %s\n", is_valid))
```

## Multi-Step Pipeline

Chain three transforms for aggressive compression: PCA reduces
dimensions, then temporal DCT compresses in time, and finally 8-bit
quantization minimizes storage.

```{r multistep}
set.seed(7)
x <- array(rnorm(6 * 6 * 6 * 30), dim = c(6, 6, 6, 30))
tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")

write_lna(x, tmp,
          transforms = c("basis", "temporal", "quant"),
          transform_params = list(
            basis = list(k = 15),
            temporal = list(kind = "dct", n_basis = 20),
            quant = list(bits = 8)
          ))

handle <- read_lna(tmp)
recon <- handle$stash$input

input_kb <- prod(dim(x)) * 4 / 1024
output_kb <- file.info(tmp)$size / 1024
cat(sprintf("Input: %.1f KB -> Output: %.1f KB (%.1fx)\n",
            input_kb, output_kb, input_kb / output_kb))
cat(sprintf("Correlation: %.4f\n",
            cor(as.vector(x), as.vector(recon))))
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
# Clean up all temp files created in this vignette
tmp_files <- ls(pattern = "^tmp")
for (f in tmp_files) {
  val <- get(f)
  if (is.character(val) && file.exists(val)) unlink(val)
}
```
